locator: LE no statement of fact can ever be, or imply, a judgment of absolute value
interpretation: 'although all judgments of relative value can be shown to be mere statements of facts, no statement of fact can ever be, or imply, a judgment of absolute value', illustrated by the omniscient person's world-book that would contain no ethical proposition.
attribution: The passage states that all judgments of relative value are mere statements of facts but that no statement of fact can be or imply a judgment of absolute value, which is the premise.
